title: Safety-net transitions mark pressure without establishing recovery or work change
source_unit: identified SIPP person, adjacent SNAP transition followed by person-month resource, earnings, hours, job, or hardship outcome

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SNAP no -> yes followed by t+1 to t+2

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric household resource-ratio context

observations.method: Fay-BRR weighted descriptive following context; SNAP transition at t to t+1 and household resource-ratio direction at t+1 to t+2, using WPFINWGT from t and 240 replicate weights.
observations.uncertainty: Selected transition triples; resource-ratio movement can reflect timing, composition, reporting, earnings, transfers, or another shock and is not a benefit-adequacy measure.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering reported SNAP receipt with valid following household resource-ratio context.
observations.counterinterpretation: A resource decline after entry is compatible with entering during need; it is not evidence that SNAP caused the decline or failed to help.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SNAP no -> yes followed by t+1 to t+2

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric person earnings and hours context

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR comparison using monthly person earnings and average weekly hours.
observations.uncertainty: Small selected person-work universe; earnings and hours are separate valid fields and do not identify pay rate, job quality, desired schedule, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering SNAP with valid following person earnings and hours context.
observations.counterinterpretation: Earnings can rise or fall for job composition, timing, reporting, or other reasons; stable hours do not establish stable pay or household security.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SNAP no -> yes followed by t+1 to t+2

denominator.unit: valid person transition triples with numeric job-count context

observations.method: Same following-context Fay-BRR comparison using monthly person job-count categories.
observations.uncertainty: Selected job-count universe; stable job count can coexist with changing hours, earnings, schedule control, care, or household resources.
observations.subgroup: Persons entering SNAP with valid following job-count context.
observations.counterinterpretation: A stable job count is not evidence of stable work quality or restored material room.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; SNAP transition followed by next-month hardship

denominator.unit: valid adjacent person-month pairs for SNAP no -> yes

observations.method: Weighted descriptive comparison from the SIPP public-use file using month-t SNAP state and month-t+1 hardship; 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR.
observations.uncertainty: Rare selected transition and separate hardship universes; the fields do not record notice, amount, gap days, remedy, or later recovery.
observations.counterinterpretation: Entry can be a marker of need rather than a cause of following hardship; hardship can persist while assistance is being used.

related_sources.claim: Resource and job-count movement occupy different monthly clocks.
Earnings direction and hours direction are separate transitions, especially by work-limiting status.
Safety-net receipt can change the route without closing the household gap.

boundary: This is a descriptive same-person SIPP transition bridge. It does not estimate SNAP effectiveness, benefit adequacy, household prevalence, work quality, causality, notice, administrative remedy, recovery, trust, political action, or a cultural or geopolitical consequence. The transition and following outcomes are selected valid universes with separate denominators.
